claims.claim: Photius was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 858 to 867 and from 877 to 886.
Photius was born c. 815 and died on 6 February 893.
Photius is recognized in the Eastern Orthodox Church as 'Saint Photius the Great'.
Photius was appointed patriarch in 858 while still a layman, succeeding Ignatius who had been unjustly deposed.

The Photian schism involved a dispute between Photius and Pope Nicholas I over Photius's legitimacy as patriarch, with Photius championing the autonomous traditions of the Eastern Church against Rome.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos was edited by Migne in Patrologia Graeca volume 101, columns 1233–1250.
A manuscript of the Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos survives in Oxford, Magdalen College, MS gr. 007, folios 55–79v.
The works of Photius known at the time were collected by Migne in Patrologia Graeca, volumes CI–CV.
